Please solve this issue:

## Bug Description

If USB CDC_ACM is selected as a logging backend and the USB cable is not connected to the board at startup, logs are flooded with 'Device not configured or suspended, drop N bytes' warnings. The logging subsystem enables backends immediately after calling their init() callback, without checking whether the backend is actually ready to receive messages.

Backends like USB CDC_ACM require additional time to become operational (e.g., waiting for a USB host connection). The assumption that the backend is always ready after init() returns is incorrect.

The logging backend API needs a mechanism for backends to indicate they are not yet ready. The logging core should defer enabling backends that report they are not ready, and periodically re-check until they become ready.

The failing test creates two backends with 500ms and 1000ms activation delays. Without a fix, both backends are enabled immediately so both receive all log messages. With the fix, backend2 should miss the first log message (it was not yet ready when it was logged), and only receive the second.

Relevant source: include/zephyr/logging/log_backend.h and subsys/logging/log_core.c

	k_timer_start(&context->timer, K_MSEC(context->delay), K_NO_WAIT);

static uint32_t max_filter_get(uint32_t filters)
{
	uint32_t max_filter = LOG_LEVEL_NONE;
	int first_slot = LOG_FILTER_FIRST_BACKEND_SLOT_IDX;
	int i;

	for (i = first_slot; i < LOG_FILTERS_NUM_OF_SLOTS; i++) {

uint32_t z_impl_log_filter_set(struct log_backend const *const backend,
			       uint32_t domain_id, int16_t source_id,
			       uint32_t level)
{
	__ASSERT_NO_MSG(source_id < (int16_t)z_log_sources_count());

	if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_LOG_RUNTIME_FILTERING)) {
		uint32_t new_aggr_filter;

		uint32_t *filters = z_log_dynamic_filters_get(source_id);

		if (backend == NULL) {
			struct log_backend const *iter_backend;
			uint32_t max = 0U;
			uint32_t current;

			for (int i = 0; i < log_backend_count_get(); i++) {
				iter_backend = log_backend_get(i);
				current = log_filter_set(iter_backend,
							 domain_id,
							 source_id, level);
				max = MAX(current, max);
			}

			level = max;
		} else {
			uint32_t max = log_filter_get(backend, domain_id,
						      source_id, false);

			level = MIN(level, MAX(max, CONFIG_LOG_OVERRIDE_LEVEL));

			LOG_FILTER_SLOT_SET(filters,
					    log_backend_id_get(backend),
					    level);

			/* Once current backend filter is updated recalculate
			 * aggregated maximal level

			new_aggr_filter = max_filter_get(*filters);

			LOG_FILTER_SLOT_SET(filters,
					    LOG_FILTER_AGGR_SLOT_IDX,
					    new_aggr_filter);
		}
	}

	return level;

{

void log_generic(struct log_msg_ids src_level, const char *fmt, va_list ap,

			backend = log_backend_get(i);

				(src_level.level <= log_filter_get(backend,

	} else {
		log_arg_t args[LOG_MAX_NARGS];
		uint32_t nargs = log_count_args(fmt);

		__ASSERT_NO_MSG(nargs < LOG_MAX_NARGS);
		for (int i = 0; i < nargs; i++) {
